625	// leakRequest is one request to drive, with the two knobs the refusal cases
626	// need: an explicit instant, so one signature can be sent twice, and a different
627	// body to sign over, so a body nobody authenticated can be sent.
628	type leakRequest struct {
629		method     string
630		path       string
631		credential string
632		body       []byte
633		at         time.Time
634		signed     []byte
635	}
636	
637	// sendTo signs a request the way contracts/http-api.md documents and drives it
638	// through the real router into w.
639	func (r *leakRun) sendTo(t *testing.T, w http.ResponseWriter, req leakRequest) {
640		t.Helper()
641	
642		if req.at.IsZero() {
643			r.tick++
644			req.at = r.base.Add(-time.Duration(r.tick) * time.Second)
645		}
646		if req.signed == nil {
647			req.signed = req.body
648		}
649		if len(req.body) > 0 {
650			r.bodies = append(r.bodies, string(req.body))
651		}
652	
653		hr := httptest.NewRequest(req.method, req.path, bytes.NewReader(req.body))
654		hr.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
655		if req.credential != "" {
656			hr.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+req.credential)
657		}
658	
659		// Computed from first principles rather than by calling the auth package's
660		// own signer, exactly as internal/httpapi's tests do it: a test that signs
661		// with the code under test proves only that the code agrees with itself.
662		ts := strconv.FormatInt(req.at.Unix(), 10)
663		mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, daemonKey())
664		// METHOD "\n" PATH "\n" timestamp "." body: the signature names the request
665		// it authorizes, not just the instant and the bytes.
666		if _, err := mac.Write([]byte(hr.Method + "\n" + hr.URL.EscapedPath() + "\n" + ts + "." + string(req.signed))); err != nil {
667			t.Fatalf("sign the request: %v", err)
668		}
669		hr.Header.Set(auth.HeaderTimestamp, ts)
670		hr.Header.Set(auth.HeaderSignature, "sha256="+hex.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil)))
671	
672		r.srv.ServeHTTP(w, hr)
673	}

675	// want drives a request and fails unless the daemon answered as expected.
676	//
677	// The response body is deliberately never printed. One of them carries the only
678	// copy of a bearer token that will ever exist, and a failing test's output is
679	// one more place for it to be.
680	func (r *leakRun) want(t *testing.T, status int, what string, req leakRequest) *httptest.ResponseRecorder {
681		t.Helper()
682	
683		got := httptest.NewRecorder()
684		r.sendTo(t, got, req)
685		if got.Code != status {
686			t.Fatalf("%s answered %d; want %d", what, got.Code, status)
687		}
688		return got
689	}

692	func (r *leakRun) create(t *testing.T, name string) (string, string) {
693		t.Helper()

695		got := r.want(t, http.StatusCreated, "POST /sessions", leakRequest{
696			method: http.MethodPost,
697			path:   "/sessions",
698			body:   jsonBody(t, map[string]string{"name": name, "work_dir": r.repo}),
699		})

717	func jsonBody(t *testing.T, v any) []byte {
718		t.Helper()
719	
720		body, err := json.Marshal(v)

727	// present drives one request through the browser door and fails unless the
728	// daemon answered as expected.
729	//
730	// It carries the assertion header and nothing else — no signature and no bearer
731	// token — which is the door's own shape (FR-012): a browser request is never
732	// refused for carrying no signature, and there is nothing else on this door for
733	// one to present. The assertion is kept whether it was admitted or refused,
734	// because a refusal is the case where the daemon is most tempted to record what
735	// it was refusing.
736	//
737	// The response body is never printed, for the reason want's is not: one of them
738	// is a whole session screen.
739	func (r *leakRun) present(t *testing.T, status int, what, path, assertion string) *httptest.ResponseRecorder {
740		t.Helper()
741	
742		// Kept once each, unlike the bodies: one assertion authorises five of the
743		// requests below, and a mark per presentation would print that same leak five
744		// times over in a failure whose whole subject is a value nobody should be
745		// looking at.
746		if !slices.Contains(r.assertions, assertion) {
747			r.assertions = append(r.assertions, assertion)
748		}
749	
750		req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, path, nil)
751		req.Header.Set(headerAssertion, assertion)
752	
753		got := httptest.NewRecorder()
754		r.srv.ServeHTTP(got, req)
755		if got.Code != status {
756			t.Fatalf("%s answered %d; want %d", what, got.Code, status)
757		}
758		return got
759	}

761	// browserAction is one mutating request to the dashboard: the route, the
762	// identity presented at layer 1, what the browser says about where the request
763	// came from, and the form it carries.
764	//
765	// A struct rather than four parameters, for the reason leakRequest is one on the
766	// other door: several of the cases below differ from an admitted one by exactly
767	// one member, and a call site naming which member is a call site that says what
768	// it is driving.
769	type browserAction struct {
770		path      string
771		assertion string
772		site      string
773		form      url.Values
774	}
775	
776	// act drives one mutating request through the browser door and fails unless the
777	// daemon answered as expected.
778	//
779	// It carries three things a read on this door never does — the fetch-metadata
780	// header the gate requires, a form-encoded body, and the page token inside it —
781	// and nothing else: no signature and no bearer token, because a browser holds
782	// neither (FR-012).
783	//
784	// The encoded body is kept whole, like the API door's, because FR-042 forbids a
785	// record built from a body and not only from the interesting parts of one. The
786	// response body is never printed, for the reason want's and present's are not.
787	func (r *leakRun) act(t *testing.T, status int, what string, action browserAction) *httptest.ResponseRecorder {
788		t.Helper()
789	
790		if !slices.Contains(r.assertions, action.assertion) {
791			r.assertions = append(r.assertions, action.assertion)
792		}
793	
794		body := action.form.Encode()
795		if body != "" {
796			r.bodies = append(r.bodies, body)
797		}
798	
799		req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, action.path, strings.NewReader(body))
800		req.Header.Set(headerAssertion, action.assertion)
801		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", contentTypeForm)
802		if action.site != "" {
803			req.Header.Set(headerFetchSite, action.site)
804		}
805	
806		got := httptest.NewRecorder()
807		r.srv.ServeHTTP(got, req)
808		if got.Code != status {
809			t.Fatalf("%s answered %d; want %d", what, got.Code, status)
810		}
811		return got
812	}

814	// The two things this suite reads back out of rendered markup.
815	//
816	// Both patterns are contracts/actions.md's own shapes rather than anything taken
817	// from the template set: a render that stopped emitting the hidden field, or a
818	// card that stopped naming its session, fails here rather than quietly leaving
819	// the sweep with nothing to look for.
820	var (
821		hiddenProof = regexp.MustCompile(`name="` + fieldProof + `" value="([^"]+)"`)
822	
823		cardDestroyForm = regexp.MustCompile(
824			fmt.Sprintf(`action="/dashboard/sessions/([0-9a-f]{%d})/destroy"`, session.IDLen))
825	)
826	
827	// proofFrom takes the page token out of a page this daemon rendered.
828	//
829	// Collected rather than computed, because it cannot be computed: the key behind
830	// it is 32 bytes read from the process's entropy at startup and served by no
831	// route, which is the property that makes the token worth sweeping for at all.
832	func (r *leakRun) proofFrom(t *testing.T, page string) string {
833		t.Helper()
834	
835		found := hiddenProof.FindStringSubmatch(page)
836		if found == nil {
837			t.Fatal("the rendered page carries no page token, so no action below could be authorised")
838		}
839		return found[1]
840	}

842	// idFrom takes a session's identifier out of a card this daemon rendered, which
843	// is how this suite learns the id of a session the browser itself created.
844	func (r *leakRun) idFrom(t *testing.T, card string) string {
845		t.Helper()
846	
847		found := cardDestroyForm.FindStringSubmatch(card)
848		if found == nil {
849			t.Fatal("the rendered card names no session, so every action below would drive nothing")
850		}
851		return found[1]
852	}

854	// driveTheActionRoutes runs the daemon through the browser door's mutating half
855	// (T021): all four actions contracts/actions.md fixes, each in the shapes that
856	// have a marked value in hand at the moment a record is written.
857	//
858	// Nothing before this proved these routes are silent. The read side was swept
859	// when the door was added, and its records are written while the daemon holds a
860	// screen and a verified address; these are written while it holds those *and*
861	// three values no read has ever had — the page token that authorised the change,
862	// the name a caller typed into a box on their own dashboard, and the command a
863	// compact delivers into a live session.
864	//
865	// Every admitted request carries a real token and says same-origin, which is
866	// AR-005 rather than convenience: a test satisfies the cross-site checks, it
867	// never disables them. The two refusals at the end fail each half deliberately,
868	// which is the other thing AR-005 asks for.
869	//
870	// The session these actions name is one the browser itself created. The API's
871	// session has to survive to the end of driveEveryOperation, and a browser
872	// destroy would end it half way through.
873	func (r *leakRun) driveTheActionRoutes(t *testing.T, assertion string) {
874		t.Helper()
875	
876		r.pageProof = r.proofFrom(t, r.fleetBody)
877		authorised := func(fields url.Values) url.Values {
878			fields.Set(fieldProof, r.pageProof)
879			return fields
880		}
881	
882		// A create, and the fleet its redirect lands on. It is the one action that
883		// mints a bearer token and hands it to nobody (FR-013) — a credential in
884		// scope with no field anywhere to hold it, which is the arrangement most
885		// likely to end with one in a record instead.
886		r.act(t, http.StatusSeeOther, "POST /dashboard/sessions", browserAction{
887			path: "/dashboard/sessions", assertion: assertion, site: siteSameOrigin,
888			form: authorised(url.Values{fieldName: {browserName}, fieldWorkDir: {r.repo}}),
889		})
890		r.createdCard = r.present(t, http.StatusOK, "the fleet a create redirected to",
891			"/?outcome=created", assertion).Body.String()
892	
893		id := r.idFrom(t, r.createdCard)
894		// A screen for it, so every later action against this session is decided by a
895		// daemon holding pane content along with everything else.
896		r.tmux.SetPane(session.Session{ID: id}.TmuxName(), paneText)
897	
898		// The two ways a create is refused, each carrying something a refusal would be
899		// tempted to quote back: a name spelled as a tmux target, and a working
900		// directory no allowlist approves.
901		r.act(t, http.StatusSeeOther, "a browser create naming a tmux target", browserAction{
902			path: "/dashboard/sessions", assertion: assertion, site: siteSameOrigin,
903			form: authorised(url.Values{fieldName: {targetName}, fieldWorkDir: {r.repo}}),
904		})
905		r.act(t, http.StatusSeeOther, "a browser create outside every approved root", browserAction{
906			path: "/dashboard/sessions", assertion: assertion, site: siteSameOrigin,
907			form: authorised(url.Values{fieldName: {browserName}, fieldWorkDir: {outsideRoot}}),
908		})
909	
910		// A rename carrying finding 408's credential-shaped name, and the fleet its
911		// redirect lands on. That page is where a caller's text is rendered back to
912		// them, so it is where a record built from what a browser was shown would be
913		// built from something a caller wrote.
914		r.act(t, http.StatusSeeOther, "POST /dashboard/sessions/{id}/rename", browserAction{
915			path: "/dashboard/sessions/" + id + "/rename", assertion: assertion, site: siteSameOrigin,
916			form: authorised(url.Values{fieldName: {hostileRename}}),
917		})
918		r.renamedCard = r.present(t, http.StatusOK, "the fleet a rename redirected to",
919			"/?outcome=renamed", assertion).Body.String()
920		r.act(t, http.StatusSeeOther, "a browser rename naming a tmux target", browserAction{
921			path: "/dashboard/sessions/" + id + "/rename", assertion: assertion, site: siteSameOrigin,
922			form: authorised(url.Values{fieldName: {targetName}}),
923		})
924	
925		// A compact. Its payload is the daemon's own and holds no secret, and it is
926		// swept all the same: contracts/actions.md forbids the delivered text from
927		// the trail whatever it happens to say, because the next payload delivered
928		// through this door may not be a constant.
929		r.act(t, http.StatusSeeOther, "POST /dashboard/sessions/{id}/compact", browserAction{
930			path: "/dashboard/sessions/" + id + "/compact", assertion: assertion, site: siteSameOrigin,
931			form: authorised(url.Values{}),
932		})
933	
934		// Typed text with Enter. The canary is the caller's own, so this is the route
935		// where a record built from what was delivered would carry something a caller
936		// wrote into a shell.
937		r.act(t, http.StatusNoContent, "POST /dashboard/sessions/{id}/type", browserAction{
938			path: "/dashboard/sessions/" + id + "/type", assertion: assertion, site: siteSameOrigin,
939			form: authorised(url.Values{"text": {canaryTyped}, "enter": {confirmYes}}),
940		})
941	
942		// One key from the bar, the route that carries a closed name where type
943		// carries text. Neither spelling of it may reach the trail.
944		r.act(t, http.StatusNoContent, "POST /dashboard/sessions/{id}/key", browserAction{
945			path: "/dashboard/sessions/" + id + "/key", assertion: assertion, site: siteSameOrigin,
946			form: authorised(url.Values{"key": {keyPressed}}),
947		})
948	
949		// And a compact the host refused, which is the only way this route reaches
950		// its fail-closed answer at all — the not-found arm beside it needs a session
951		// that vanished between two reads of the store. It is worth driving twice
952		// over: the error tmux hands back carries pane-shaped text, so the daemon is
953		// holding *both* the delivered command and something it did not author while
954		// it decides what to record.
955		r.tmux.FailOp(tmuxctl.OpPaste, errHostError)
956		r.act(t, http.StatusSeeOther, "a browser compact the host refused", browserAction{
957			path: "/dashboard/sessions/" + id + "/compact", assertion: assertion, site: siteSameOrigin,
958			form: authorised(url.Values{}),
959		})
960		r.tmux.FailOp(tmuxctl.OpPaste, nil)
961	
962		// A destroy without the confirming step, and then with it. The first is the
963		// one refusal on this door that tears nothing down (FR-029); the second ends
964		// the session this function created.
965		r.act(t, http.StatusSeeOther, "a browser destroy that was not confirmed", browserAction{
966			path: "/dashboard/sessions/" + id + "/destroy", assertion: assertion, site: siteSameOrigin,
967			form: authorised(url.Values{}),
968		})
969		r.act(t, http.StatusSeeOther, "POST /dashboard/sessions/{id}/destroy", browserAction{
970			path: "/dashboard/sessions/" + id + "/destroy", assertion: assertion, site: siteSameOrigin,
971			form: authorised(url.Values{fieldConfirm: {confirmYes}}),
972		})
973	
974		// An action against an identifier this daemon never minted, which is the
975		// uniform not-found three of the four routes share.
976		r.act(t, http.StatusNotFound, "a browser compact of a session that never existed", browserAction{
977			path:      "/dashboard/sessions/" + strings.Repeat("e", session.IDLen) + "/compact",
978			assertion: assertion, site: siteSameOrigin, form: authorised(url.Values{}),
979		})
980	
981		// The gate refusing, in each half separately (FR-002c). Both hold a
982		// caller-authored value while they decide — the fetch-metadata header a

1428		// The page token this daemon really minted. It is added here rather than
1429		// listed above because it is the one swept value the daemon authored instead
1430		// of the fixture: the key behind it is read from the process's entropy at
1431		// startup, so no constant could name it and the render is the only place it
1432		// can be collected from.
1433		if r.pageProof != "" {
1434			marks = append(marks, leakMark{"the page token a render handed a browser", r.pageProof})
1435		}
1436	
1437		for _, credential := range r.credentials {
1438			hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(credential))

1447		// the two are different claims: a record built from a body that happened to
1448		// carry nothing marked would still be a record carrying a body.
1449		for i, body := range r.bodies {
1450			marks = append(marks, leakMark{fmt.Sprintf("request body %d, whole", i+1), body})
1451		}
1452	
1453		// The assertions, whole and segment by segment. Whole is the claim FR-035
1454		// makes; the segments are what catches the narrower leak — a record built
1455		// from the payload alone would carry every claim the edge wrote, base64 and
1456		// therefore unmatched by any mark above, since none of the values inside it
1457		// survives the encoding as text.
1458		for i, assertion := range r.assertions {
1459			marks = append(marks, leakMark{fmt.Sprintf("assertion %d, whole", i+1), assertion})
1460			for _, part := range strings.Split(assertion, ".") {
1461				marks = append(marks, leakMark{fmt.Sprintf("one segment of assertion %d", i+1), part})

1463		}

1467	// lines is everything the run wrote, from both sinks.
1468	func (r *leakRun) lines() []leakLine {
1469		var out []leakLine
1470		for _, text := range strings.Split(r.trail.String(), "\n") {
1471			if text != "" {
1472				out = append(out, leakLine{from: "the audit trail", text: text})
1473			}
1474		}
1475		for _, text := range strings.Split(r.logs.String(), "\n") {
1476			if text != "" {
1477				out = append(out, leakLine{from: "the daemon's log output", text: text})
1478			}
1479		}
1480		return out
1481	}

1483	// records decodes the audit trail, which also asserts that every line of it is
1484	// one JSON object — the shape an operator's `journalctl | jq` depends on.
1485	func (r *leakRun) records(t *testing.T) []map[string]any {
1486		t.Helper()
1487	
1488		var out []map[string]any
1489		for _, line := range strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(r.trail.String()), "\n") {
1490			if line == "" {
1491				continue
1492			}
1493			var rec map[string]any
1494			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &rec); err != nil {
1495				t.Fatalf("an audit line is not JSON: %v (%q)", err, line)
1496			}
1497			out = append(out, rec)
1498		}
1499		return out
1500	}
1501	
1502	// pasted is the prompt as it reached the host: the payload of the load-buffer
1503	// call, which is the one place caller text is supposed to end up.
1504	func (r *leakRun) pasted(t *testing.T) string {
1505		t.Helper()
1506	
1507		var payloads []string
1508		for _, call := range r.tmux.Calls() {
1509			if (call.Op == tmuxctl.OpPaste || call.Op == tmuxctl.OpPasteBracketed) && len(call.Stdin) > 0 {
1510				payloads = append(payloads, string(call.Stdin))
1511			}
1512		}
1513		if len(payloads) == 0 {
1514			t.Fatal("nothing was ever pasted into a session")
1515		}
1516		return strings.Join(payloads, "\n")
1517	}
1518	
1519	// keysSent is every key name the host was asked to press, as tmux spells them.
1520	func (r *leakRun) keysSent(t *testing.T) string {
1521		t.Helper()
1522	
1523		var argv []string
1524		for _, call := range r.tmux.Calls() {
1525			if call.Op == tmuxctl.OpSendKeys {
1526				argv = append(argv, strings.Join(call.Argv, " "))
1527			}
1528		}
1529		if len(argv) == 0 {
1530			t.Fatal("no key was ever sent to a session")
1531		}
1532		return strings.Join(argv, "\n")
1533	}
1534	
1535	// TestNoOperationLeaksSecretMaterialIntoTheTrailOrTheLogs is FR-042 and SC-013
1536	// stated across the whole daemon: drive everything it can do with values chosen
1537	// to be unmistakable, then read back everything it wrote and find none of them.
1538	//
1539	// Not parallel: driveEveryOperation redirects the process's standard logger,
1540	// which is the only way to see what the daemon writes when its own last-resort
1541	// channel is all that is left.
1542	func TestNoOperationLeaksSecretMaterialIntoTheTrailOrTheLogs(t *testing.T) {
1543		run := driveEveryOperation(t)
1544	
1545		lines := run.lines()
1546		if len(lines) == 0 {
1547			t.Fatal("the run produced no output at all, so there is nothing here that could have leaked")
1548		}
1549	
1550		for _, mark := range run.marks() {
1551			for i, line := range lines {
1552				if strings.Contains(line.text, mark.value) {
1553					// The leaked line is printed because that is what an operator
1554					// would need to see; by this point the value is already out.
1555					t.Errorf("%s appears in %s, line %d — FR-042 forbids it:\n\t%s", mark.what, line.from, i+1, line.text)
1556				}
1557			}
1558		}
1559	}
1560	
1561	// TestTheLeakSuiteReallyDrivesTheDaemon is what keeps the sweep above honest.
1562	//
1563	// A suite that quietly stopped exercising the daemon would keep passing, and
1564	// would keep passing for exactly as long as nobody looked — which is the failure
1565	// mode a leak test has and an ordinary test does not, because its assertion is
1566	// an absence. So: every action the trail can carry appeared, and every marked
1567	// value provably reached the place it was supposed to reach.
1568	func TestTheLeakSuiteReallyDrivesTheDaemon(t *testing.T) {
1569		run := driveEveryOperation(t)
1570	
1571		// data-model.md's and contracts/http-api.md's spellings, written out rather
1572		// than read back from the audit package's constants: a test that took them
1573		// from the code would prove only that the code agrees with itself.
1574		want := []string{
1575			"startup.adopt",
1576			"session.create", "session.list", "session.detail",
1577			"session.prompt", "session.output", "session.destroy",
1578			"auth.reject", "reaper.destroy",
1579			// The browser door's four (T021c). access.reject is deliberately not
1580			// auth.reject: the two doors fail for unrelated reasons, and a sweep that
1581			// accepted either would pass on a run where layer 1 never refused
1582			// anything at all.
1583			"dashboard.view", "dashboard.asset", "access.reject", "route.unknown",
1584			// And the live stream (T029), which is the browser door's fifth and the
1585			// only record in this list written while the daemon is mid-response.
1586			"stream.open",
1587			// The mutating half's own (T021). dashboard.reject is deliberately in this
1588			// list beside access.reject: the two are the same door refusing at two
1589			// different depths, and a sweep that accepted either would pass on a run
1590			// where the action gate never refused anything at all.
1591			"dashboard.create", "dashboard.destroy", "dashboard.rename", "dashboard.compact",
1592			"dashboard.type", "dashboard.key", "dashboard.reject",
1593			// And the fleet stream, which is the second record in this list written
1594			// while the daemon is mid-response — and the only one written by a handler
1595			// that is about to stay open.
1596			"fleet.open",
1597		}
1598		got := make(map[string]bool)
1599		for _, rec := range run.records(t) {
1600			action, ok := rec["action"].(string)
1601			if !ok {
1602				t.Fatalf("an audit record carries no action: %v", rec)
1603			}
1604			got[action] = true
1605		}
1606		for _, action := range want {
1607			if !got[action] {
1608				t.Errorf("the run emitted no %s record, so the sweep proves nothing about that operation", action)
1609			}
1610		}
1611	
1612		for _, reached := range []struct {
1613			what  string
1614			mark  string
1615			where string
1616			text  string
1617		}{
1618			{"the prompt text", markPrompt, "the payload that reached the host", run.pasted(t)},
1619			{"the pane content", markPane, "the output response", run.outputBody},
1620			{"the session name", markName, "the create response", run.createBody},
1621			{"the host's own error", markHostError, "the error a failed sweep returned", run.sweptError},
1622			// The browser door's own three. Each is a value the door had in scope
1623			// while it wrote a record, and the page proves it: a dashboard that
1624			// rendered none of them would make the sweep's silence about this door
1625			// mean nothing.
1626			{"the verified address", markEmail, "the fleet page", run.fleetBody},
1627			{"the session name", markName, "the fleet page", run.fleetBody},
1628			{"the pane content", markPane, "the session's own page", run.viewBody},
1629			// The live stream's own screen, which is the value the record written at
1630			// its open was holding when it was written.
1631			{"the pane content", markPane, "the live output stream", run.streamBody},
1632			// The mutating half's own two (T021). A rename is the one action that
1633			// renders a caller's text back into its answer, and a compact is the one
1634			// that puts daemon-authored text into a live session — so these are the
1635			// two values the action routes had that no read on this door ever holds.
1636			{"a credential-shaped session name", markName, "the card a rename rendered back", run.renamedCard},
1637			{"the compact command", compactDelivered, "the payload that reached the host", run.pasted(t)},
1638			{"the typed text", canaryTyped, "the payload that reached the host", run.pasted(t)},
1639			{"the pressed key", keyPressedTmux, "the send-keys that reached the host", run.keysSent(t)},
1640		} {
1641			if !strings.Contains(reached.text, reached.mark) {
1642				t.Errorf("%s never reached %s, so its absence from the trail proves nothing", reached.what, reached.where)
1643			}
1644		}
1645	
1646		// The page token, which is the one swept value the daemon authored. Its
1647		// evidence is that a render put it on a page and a handler wrote it back into
1648		// a card — and, above that, that every admitted action carried it and none of
1649		// them was refused, which driveTheActionRoutes already asserted.
1650		//
1651		// **The two renders are not asserted to carry the same bytes**, and that was a
1652		// latent fragility here rather than a property. A page token is
1653		// `expiry + mac` where expiry is `now.Add(12h).Unix()` — one-second
1654		// granularity — so two renders that land either side of a second boundary
1655		// carry different tokens, legitimately. This passed for as long as a create
1656		// happened to fit inside one second and began failing the moment anything on
1657		// that path grew slower, which is a test measuring the clock rather than the
1658		// daemon.
1659		//
1660		// What has to be true is what is checked instead: the swept value really came
1661		// off a rendered page (it did — proofFrom fatals otherwise, and every action
1662		// below was admitted carrying it), and a create's own page really carries one
1663		// too.
1664		if run.pageProof == "" {
1665			t.Error("no page token was ever rendered, so the sweep proves nothing about one")
1666		} else if !hiddenProof.MatchString(run.createdCard) {
1667			t.Error("the page a create redirected to carries no page token at all, so the sweep is reading a value the daemon never put on a page")
1668		}
1669	
1670		// The pane's escape sequences live inside the pane content the rows above
1671		// already prove reached the output response and both streams. This is the
1672		// fixture checking itself: an edit that took the escapes out of paneText
1673		// would leave two marks in the sweep that nothing ever produced.
1674		if !strings.Contains(paneText, paneEscapeRaw) {
1675			t.Error("the fixture's pane content carries no escape sequences, so the sweep's silence about them proves nothing")
1676		}
1677	
1678		// And that the JSON spelling really is the one an encoder produces. A mark
1679		// nothing could ever match is a mark that passes for ever; encoding the raw
1680		// sequence is what tells the two apart.
1681		encoded, err := json.Marshal(paneEscapeRaw)
1682		if err != nil {
1683			t.Fatalf("encode the pane's escape sequences: %v", err)
1684		}
1685		if !strings.Contains(string(encoded), paneEscapeJSON) {
1686			t.Errorf("a JSON encoder writes the pane's escape sequences as %s, not as %q; the sweep is looking for a spelling nothing produces",
1687				encoded, paneEscapeJSON)
1688		}
1689	
1690		if len(run.credentials) == 0 {
1691			t.Error("no bearer token was ever issued, so the sweep proves nothing about one")
1692		}
1693		if len(run.bodies) == 0 {
1694			t.Error("no request body was ever sent, so the sweep proves nothing about one")
1695		}
1696		if len(run.assertions) == 0 {
1697			t.Error("no assertion was ever presented, so the sweep proves nothing about one")
1698		}
1699		if run.logs.Len() == 0 {
1700			t.Error("the run produced no log output, so the sweep read only the audit sink")
1701		}
1702	}
